column4: dialect-gated per SUBTEST: a registeredBackends test, so it runs one subtest per dialect and mysql and mssql skip in these PostgreSQL-only jobs while postgres RUNS -- two, not three. Measured by name rather than by delta, with CLEAT_TEST_MYSQL and CLEAT_TEST_MSSQL unset: go test -p 1 -count=1 -json ./engine/... | grep '"Action":"skip"' reports exactly these two arms. Guards cleat#1118: a completed run records which worker took it terminal. The arms have to exist even where they skip, because the write is 27 SEPARATE hand-written statements across engine/store_lifecycle.go, engine/store_admin.go, engine/db.go, engine/mysql_lifecycle.go, engine/mysql_ops.go, engine/mssql_lifecycle.go and engine/mssql_operations.go -- not one shared builder -- so a postgres-only run cannot vouch for the other two. And the ORDER within SET is genuinely per-dialect: MySQL evaluates assignments left to right and later ones see earlier ones, so `SET assigned_to = NULL, completed_by = assigned_to` records NULL on mysql while postgres and mssql both record the worker -- measured, not recalled. A postgres-only run is blind to exactly the divergence this test exists to catch.

dialect-gated per SUBTEST: same test, same two arms, and the cluster job runs ./engine/... too, so these two lines move together -- scripts/skip-ledger.d/README.md and WORKSTREAM.md both say so, and updating only one is what costs a second CI round trip. Same measurement and same reason as the test-go/engine line above; see cleat#1118.
